You really don't have to invest that much time, to have fun with learning to play and then playing.

If you can throw a half-hour per day at it, you're doing well. As you're an adult, and presumably employed, I'd suggest something like 30 minutes a day and 1 hour per day on the weekends. That might seem like a lot of time, but you'll find that it flies by.

Those times are for the duration of practice and that's different than playing the guitar. You'll find yourself playing the guitar even beyond that time. You can practice playing a song, but that's different than just playing the song. By practice, I mean drills and learning new techniques.

You'd probably also find yourself wanting to practice more than that. What you can do is play silently. Instead of plugging in, or even strumming, you can watch television while your fingers run the scales and practice chord shapes and changing chord positions. This is actually a good thing, because you're distracted by the television and you'll learn to do it as muscle memory - that is without much thought. Most of guitar is, in fact, muscle memory.

You don't really need to devote two hours per day to practice and another two hours to play and/or rehearse for the coming show. You don't have to do all that, if your goal is just to have fun and maybe entertain a few people. Even better, the guitar has opened so many doors for me. I've experienced so many things that I'd have not experienced. You get to do things like jam with people and learn from them while you're having a good time - often while inebriated.

Your goal doesn't have to be absolute guitar mastery. Your goal can be to simply learn a few chords and a few songs. Your goal can be just to have fun.

On that last bit, I suggest everyone have the goal of having fun. Even if you're also trying to truly master it, you're still better off also trying to have fun. And, it is fun. It's a lot of fun. It's healthy, rewarding, and educational.

Full disclosure: I'm obviously biased and very interested in helping people decide to learn to play a musical instrument. It's a great hobby.
